options.content:
**Dynamic Mapper service has no `/actuator/prometheus` endpoint** — metrics are pushed via OTLP to Grafana Alloy (`otel.instrumentation.micrometer.enabled=true`). The exact Prometheus metric names your Alloy/Mimir pipeline produces for the Timer-based panels below (*Processing Time*, *C8Y Processing Time*) depend on your collector's unit-suffix setting:
- This dashboard assumes **no unit infix**: `<name>_sum`, `<name>_count`, `<name>_bucket`.
- If your pipeline adds one, the real names will be `<name>_milliseconds_sum/_count/_bucket` or `<name>_seconds_sum/_count/_bucket`.
- Open **Explore** on the `$datasource` variable's datasource and search the metrics browser for `dynmapper_inbound_processing_time` to confirm, then edit the affected panel queries.

**CPU Utilization** is not a custom metric emitted by this service's own code (no Spring Boot Actuator / `micrometer-registry-prometheus` dependency exists). The CPU panels query the OTel Java runtime-telemetry metric `jvm_cpu_recent_utilization` that this service enables (`otel.instrumentation.runtime-telemetry.enabled=true`). Alloy may append a `_ratio` unit suffix, and older instrumentation versions use `process_runtime_jvm_cpu_utilization`, so the query matches all of these names plus Micrometer's `process_cpu_usage`. Verify in your metrics browser which one exists and narrow the `__name__` regex if you like.

**Outbound identity cache hit rate** cannot be shown as a percentage — the code only counts outbound cache *hits* (`dynmapper_outbound_identity_cache_hits_total`); there is no outbound "total lookups" counter to divide by (unlike the inbound path). Only the hit rate (count/sec) is shown for outbound.

**C8Y Processing Time** and **Available C8Y Connections** are process-wide metrics without tenant or connector labels, so only the Instance selector filters them. The JVM panels (CPU, heap, metaspace) and the version tile are also filtered by Instance only.

panels.description: Information only: the service version reported by the selected instance (dynmapper_build_info). Does not filter the other panels.
panels.title: Deployed Version (selected instance)
Outbound Identity Cache Hits/sec (no denominator metric exists)

panels.description: Process CPU utilization of the selected instance, 0 to 1. Not a custom metric from this codebase: it comes from the OpenTelemetry runtime telemetry (jvm.cpu.recent_utilization), with the older OpenTelemetry and Micrometer names as fallbacks. See Setup Notes.
panels.title: CPU Utilization

panels.description: Micrometer jvm_memory_used_bytes, of the selected instance. Standard Micrometer metric, not a custom metric from this codebase.
panels.title: Heap Used

panels.description: Micrometer jvm_memory_used_bytes for the Metaspace pool, of the selected instance.
panels.title: Metaspace Used

panels.description: Micrometer jvm_memory_used_bytes for all non-heap pools (Metaspace, code cache, compressed class space), of the selected instance.
panels.title: Non-heap Used

panels.description: Micrometer jvm_memory_used_bytes per scrape instance. Heap is the sum of its pools; metaspace is the Metaspace pool. One line per instance shows whether a high value comes from many instances or one.
panels.title: Memory Over Time (per instance)

panels.description: Process CPU (jvm.cpu.recent_utilization) and whole-host CPU where the runtime reports it, 0 to 1 for the selected instance. Not custom metrics from this codebase: they come from the OpenTelemetry runtime telemetry, with the older OpenTelemetry and Micrometer names as fallbacks.
panels.title: CPU Over Time (per instance)

panels.description: Share of inbound messages whose processing resulted in at least one error, over the selected range.
panels.title: Inbound Error Ratio (selected range)

panels.description: Share of outbound messages whose processing resulted in at least one error, over the selected range.
panels.title: Outbound Error Ratio (selected range)
Error Rate Over Time by Connector

panels.description: Current status per connector. Value mapping: 0=UNKNOWN, 1=CONFIGURED, 2=ENABLED, 3=CONNECTING, 4=CONNECTED, 5=DISCONNECTED, 6=DISCONNECTING, 7=FAILED, 8=RETRYING.
panels.title: Connector Status

panels.description: Connectors currently reporting FAILED (ordinal 7). Alert on this being > 0.
panels.title: Connectors Currently FAILED

panels.description: Mappings that hold de-duplication fingerprints now (they call $isDuplicate or context.isDuplicate). A mapping with no traffic for one window drops out. Deduplicated across replicas.
panels.title: Mappings Using De-duplication

panels.description: Fingerprints held now, including expired ones not yet removed by the once-a-minute cleanup.
panels.title: Fingerprints Held

panels.description: Estimated heap of the fingerprints (entries x 150 bytes). An estimate, not a measurement. Each replica holds its own copy, so this is the largest replica, not the sum.
panels.title: De-duplication Memory (estimated)

panels.description: Messages dropped as repeats. Summed over replicas.
panels.title: Repeats Dropped/sec

panels.description: Mappings, estimated memory, and drop rate per tenant. Memory is on the left axis in bytes.
panels.title: De-duplication Over Time by Tenant

panels.description: Messages processed without a duplicate check because a de-duplication store was full (limit mapping or total). Repeats are not dropped while this is above 0. Summed over replicas.
panels.title: Checks Skipped (store full)/sec

list.description: Scrape instance (pod or replica) serving the selected tenant. Memory and CPU are per instance, so select exactly one.
list.label: Instance
list.name: instance
